verdict.rationale: Asana documents a formal deprecation process: a clear description of each change, a migration plan, a deprecation period where old and new behavior coexist, Asana-Change response headers warning of upcoming changes, and Asana-Enable/Disable headers to opt in or out per request. The evidence does not show explicit versioning of the REST API itself; change management works through per-feature header toggles rather than documented API version identifiers. missing for 10: explicit API version numbering/versioning scheme documented, stated deprecation timelines/durations, independent or hands-on corroboration of the deprecation process.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can rely on versioned APIs with a documented deprecation policy

citations.quote: We will designate a deprecation period during which you will be able to choose between both old and new behavior from the API, allowing you to test out the change without having to put your entire app at risk.
Shortly after we post communication, the API will begin sending Asana-Change headers in the responses.

Sending an `Asana-Enable` header including comma-separated names of features will turn those features on for that request. Sending an `Asana-Disable` header will do the opposite and turn those features off for that request.
Apps you write on top of the API now should, in ideal situations, continue to work indefinitely.
